gap: No result ChatGPT got states that an "8 TB" NAS with drives can mean very different usable space: Synology's BeeStation Plus 8 TB (one drive, no RAID) gives about 6.98 TB usable, while Buffalo's LinkStation 720D 8 TB is 2 × 4 TB set to RAID 1 at the factory, so only 4 TB (decimal) holds files.
standout_why: ChatGPT's saved chat has no result pages at all, so no cited rival covers this. Its answer showed two product cards, Synology DS224+ and UGREEN DXP4800 Plus. Both are sold without drives: Synology says 'Storage drives are sold separately', and UGREEN's store sells the DXP4800 Plus as the bare unit for $619.99. Its 4–8 / 8–16 / 20–40 TB chips never say whether TB means raw or usable. Our current page shows usable space only for the two BeeStations (6.98 and 3.45). For the LinkStation it says '2 × 4 TB, RAID preconfigured' without the usable figure.
decides: For a shopper who picks by the TB number on the box, the mirrored Buffalo 8 TB stores about half of what the BeeStation Plus 8 TB stores. That half is the cost of a second copy of every file; the BeeStation has none, and Synology itself says 'Data safety comes from backups, not RAID'. The table needs a 'usable TB' column and a footnote. It should also point out that neither product ChatGPT showed includes any storage. Without verified prices for the drive-included units, this finding cannot settle cost per usable TB.

findings.label: Usable capacity vs labelled capacity
findings.value: 8 TB labelled, about 6.98 usable (no unit given beyond 'TB'); 1 drive, no RAID
findings.note: Page quote: 'The actual usable capacity is approximately 6.98 for 8 TB.' FAQ: 'only one built-in hard drive (no RAID)' and 'Data safety comes from backups, not RAID.' 6.98/8 = 87% of the label. Warranty 3 years. The page showed no price.

findings.label: Usable capacity vs labelled capacity
findings.value: 4 TB labelled, about 3.45 TB usable; 1 drive, no RAID; 2 GB DDR4; 1GbE
findings.note: Page quote: 'Actual usable capacity for 4 TB is approximately 3.45 TB.' 3.45/4 = 86%. This is a newer model than the BST150-4T on our current page, which has 1 GB of RAM (same page wording). Warranty 3 years. The page showed no price.

findings.label: Drive layout and factory RAID mode
findings.value: 4 TB × 2, set to RAID 1 at the factory → 4 TB (decimal) usable for files
findings.source_title: Buffalo Japan – LS720D0802 product spec sheet (print view)
findings.note: Page quotes: 'LS720D0802：4TB×2'; RAID modes 'RAID 1 / RAID 0 / 通常モード'; '※出荷時はRAID 1に設定されています' (ships set to RAID 1). The maker states no usable figure, so the 4 TB comes from my arithmetic: a RAID 1 mirror stores one drive's worth. That is about 3.64 TiB before filesystem overhead, so roughly half of what the BeeStation Plus 8 TB stores in Synology's units. Released November 2020. The Japanese page gives a 1-year warranty, which may not match US terms.
